expect.why: the `## Passages` section is last, below the APPEND marker, and its one block is well formed: an ISO 8601 timestamp no earlier than the entry, an author who may write, and a witness stated by value
the witness digests to the Observation section as commit 01 held it, and the held prose is a contiguous run of that section

the lift left the citing sentence in the section it was in, so the sentence that states the claim and the span the claim rests on are still one span — which is what `citation-placement` asks, and it is on in this corpus
the lift moved the section the ground is anchored to, and the reading verdict at commit 02 states the digest of the section as the lift left it

note: the shape every other passage seed is a deformation of: prose lifted out of an artifact at commit 02, the citation left where it was, the witness naming the section as commit 01 held it, and a reading verdict discharging the drift the lift itself caused. Three things are held here at once and no earlier seed holds any of them: a `## Passages` section is optional, so every other seed in this corpus is a near-negative for the optionality rule and this one is the positive; the citation stays inside the span the ground pins, so `references` and the placement rule are both asked about a section prose has just been taken out of; and the ground is anchored by value over text that carries an entry id, which is only stable because the corpus re-derives anchors under a rename.
history: apply commits/01, commits/02, … as successive commits in a fresh repository; expectations name the commit they apply to. `@commitNN` in an entry is substituted with the real short object id of that commit before it is made, because a seed cannot know an id the runner has not created yet
